Seen this all over social media and finally got around to trying it out. To start off, this is Valet only. When I went it was $20, so just know this before going. The atmosphere and aesthetic to the location is really nice. You can sit indoor or outside. The inside has cushion chairs which were really close to each other with very limited space to get in or out without bumping into the person behind you.
Now for the food review. We got the crispy spicy tuna, garlic noodles with steak (medium rare), baked lobster roll, oysters and the ribeye. The garlic noodles were very dry, lacking a lot of flavor, the steak carried this dish. The oysters were good, would recommend the half dozen. The baked lobster roll was delicious, definitely my favorite, the dynamite sauce added a great flavor to the lobster. The crispy spicy tuna was also very delicious, it does pack a bit of heat, such a delicious wow factor.  The steak was on the weak side. The sauce it was smothered on didnt really help it, but it made the carrots it paired with delicious. I wish they offered more sides as the mashed potatoes were also not that great. Overall the  quality of food is quite average for the amount of options available in LA. If this restaurant was somewhere  other than LA I would understand why the cost is so high, feels like you're  been more so sold on the aesthetic,view, and history of the building more than the quality of food.

Our server was Nick and he was amazing!!  We will for sure be back.

My wife and I finally had the opportunity to dine at Musso & Frank, and the experience exceeded every expectation we had.

We had an 8:30 PM reservation, and although they had already sold out of the famous prime rib, our waiter Robert recommended the bone-in pork chop instead. It turned out to be an outstanding recommendation—perfectly cooked, incredibly flavorful, and one of the best pork chops I’ve had.

My wife ordered the scallops, and they were absolutely phenomenal. We both agreed they were some of the best scallops we’ve ever had.

Of course, we couldn’t leave without trying the famous dirty martini, and it absolutely lived up to its reputation. It paired perfectly with the meal and is a must-order for anyone visiting.

We finished the evening with the crème brûlée, which was easily among the best we’ve ever had. The caramelized sugar had the perfect crack, and the custard was rich, smooth, and beautifully balanced.

What truly made the evening special was the service. Robert was attentive, knowledgeable, and happy to answer every question we had without ever making us feel rushed. His recommendations made an already memorable dinner even better.

From the classic atmosphere to the exceptional food and impeccable hospitality, it’s easy to understand why Musso & Frank has remained a Los Angeles institution for more than a century.

This won’t be our last visit. Thank you to Robert and the entire team for an unforgettable evening.

★★★★★

It's dark and was bustling when we arrived, but conversation was easy. When the show at the Pantages started, more than half of the restaurant left.  We were one of 2 tables by 830 pm on a Tuesday night.

Excellent pre-show dining, and while not perfect, we'd return.

text.text:
Worth the Stop. Worth Going Back.

After spending a surprisingly fun afternoon wandering through Madame Tussauds, the family found ourselves debating where to grab lunch. We were considering the Hard Rock Cafe and a couple of other nearby options when the Madame Tussauds Rooftop Bar & Restaurant appeared almost by accident.

Sometimes those spontaneous decisions end up being the best ones.

This was one of them.

The food was very good, and the menu offered several appetizers that were a little different from the usual tourist fare. Everything was well prepared, thoughtfully presented, and arrived exactly as it should.

The seating is worth mentioning because it gives you a good sense of what this venue is designed to be. It’s more lounge than traditional restaurant, making it ideal for couples, small groups, or an evening out. With a family and several kids, it wasn’t quite as comfortable as a conventional dining room would have been, but everyone still settled in just fine. My impression is that this space really comes alive later in the evening rather than during lunch.

One of my favorite touches was something completely unexpected.

Scattered throughout the rooftop were wax figures posed as though they were fellow patrons, relaxing with friends and enjoying the restaurant. More than once I caught myself doing a double take before realizing I was looking at another remarkably realistic figure. It fit perfectly with the museum downstairs and added a fun bit of personality to the experience.

Our server, Jasmine, was outstanding. Friendly, attentive, and professional throughout the meal.

Just as impressive was the floor manager, whose name I unfortunately didn’t catch. She was constantly moving through the restaurant, quietly checking on guests and stepping in whenever needed to keep service flowing smoothly. Most diners probably never noticed everything she was doing, which is often the mark of someone who is exceptionally good at hospitality.

Good food, excellent service, a unique atmosphere, and a fun extension of the Madame Tussauds experience made this an easy recommendation.

If you’re already visiting the museum, don’t overlook what’s upstairs.

Worth the Stop. Worth Going Back.

I'm skeptical when I see a heavily 5-star reviewed bar or restaurant. Either the reviewer knows the owner or has some stake in the business. Indeed, I have talked to the owner but only because he makes a personal effort to connect with the community and those who frequent his place and I do have stake in the business  because I personally want to see deserving worker and arts-friendly businesses thrive in a post-COVID Hollywood economy.

I'm a community organizer for several groups and businesses in the arts & entertainment industry. The Tribute, its Staff and Owner have always demonstrated themselves to be friendly and extremely accommodating when I seek to host an event there. Attendees always have a good time, enjoying the Hollywood atmosphere and prompt service. The food and drinks are affordably priced while staying inspired and savory.

The layout accommodates the smallest or largest of groups, allowing you to enjoy your company and conversation while also feeling part of a larger tapestry of the Hollywood nightlife.

During the slower parts of the day, they've even accommodated my request to move tables and allow the display of art brought in by attendees. Indeed, the Tribute has repeatedly shown itself to be a friend to and supporter of the Arts and, importantly, Entertainment Unions.

Additionally, he and his business repeatedly demonstrate support of the LGBTQIA+ and marginalized communities.

Parking is really the only thing I have to think twice about when considering this venue for an event, with some people often choosing to park at the nearby Cinerama Dome.  I tend to take the Metro Rail in and walk over from the Hollywood/Vine station, enjoying the texture and, err, smells of Hollywood along the walk.

It doesn't matter how small or how large the group, I and my guests always feel welcomed and cared for and that's why it's one of my top go-to's when I absolutely need to make sure people have a nice night out in good company.

For those single people seeking some attractive strangers, this place also attracts them in droves, providing a friendly, beautiful and cheery environment that makes it easy for you to find each other.

text.text:
I randomly picked a breakfast spot near the hotel, and it was surprisingly delicious!!!

Breakfast Sandwich: Simple, classic ingredients, yet a dreamlike flavor. Made to order, the bacon was crispy but not hard, the avocado puree was smooth and fragrant, the vegetables were crisp and juicy, and the soft-boiled egg and cheese were perfectly runny; but the most beautiful part was the toast itself—crispy on the outside, soft on the inside, and with each bite, the slightly charred edges gently cracked open—it was simply divine.

Breakfast Burrito: I chose the non-spicy avocado salsa (green sauce). The tortilla was soft yet chewy, the egg and bacon were aromatic, and the potatoes and pinto beans were delicate and firm. It had a slight spiciness, but not overpowering. The sauce was mainly tangy, which helped cut through the richness. Overall, it was pretty good, very filling, but definitely not as good as the Breakfast Sandwich.

Iced Latte, Iced Matcha Latte: The coffee was just average, but the portion was big! The latte was better than the matcha latte, the latter was a bit bitter.

text.text:
A French fusion brunch restaurant near LACMA, a Michelin-starred establishment. The building, constructed in 1929, was once Charlie Chaplin's studio. It was packed on Saturday noon, with queues stretching dozens of meters, so I had to get takeout to eat at the museum.

Kimchi Fried Rice: Unsurprisingly one of the most popular dishes. Even as takeout, it was still incredibly flavorful. The rice was dry and fluffy, each grain distinct, perfectly absorbing the sweet, sour, and slightly spicy flavors of the kimchi; the beef short ribs were tender and juicy, with a rich, fatty aroma. The perfectly runny soft-boiled egg was a definite plus. It somewhat shattered my stereotype about Korean fried rice.

Short Rib Burrito: Calling this tortilla soaked in sauce a "burrito" is quite creative… avocado, soft-boiled egg, cheese, and black beans—a typical Mexican recipe; the sauce was tangy and spicy, refreshing and stimulating, creating a good balance with the rich, rounded flavors of the ingredients. For Cantonese like me, it was a bit too spicy.

Basque Cheesecake: Absolutely delicious...the best Basque cheesecake I've ever had! The cake was delicate and smooth, with a different texture in every bite, from the molten center to the firmer edges, and the transitions were very natural; the cheese was incredibly rich and creamy, almost like eating milk powder.

While visiting Los Angeles, I had heard about this popular restaurant located in the mid-Wilshire area serving a variety of French inspired dishes and garnering high praises from visitors.

I ordered the escargot, dover sole, salmon, prawns, fries and risotto.  Although, some dishes were good the majority were disappointing and totally missed the mark.

The Salmon was lukewarm and was sent back. The Prawns were without question the biggest disappointment. By far these were the smallest prawns I've ever had anywhere and for the price one would've truly expected more.

Overall, the meal was good but not great. The service was poor and lacked structure, creating a chaotic and rushed atmosphere.

Throughout my entire dining experience and other than the times of me personally calling over my server, he was inattentive, lacked personality and never made me feel welcomed.

Although, it appeared the staff worked as a team it never seemed cohesive and what one might expect from an establishment of this caliber.

The restaurant was crowded but I did see several staffers seemingly with little to do, which is why the lack of table service surprised me.

Kudos, to the manager who did walk over and apologized for the salmon and provided me with a $50.00 gift card towards a future visit. This was very thoughtful and appreciated.

I recently checked out BOA restaurant during Dine LA and went with their 3-course with dessert. The starter menu is a total visual experience! I ordered the Hamachi Crudo, which comes with a cool touch of smoke that lasts until your very last bite (check out my pictures!). My husband went with the Caesar salad, and let me tell you—it is truly legendary, just like the menu promises. Kenneth was amazing; he put on a fantastic three-minute performance making the Caesar salad, explaining all the ingredients and mixing the dressing right tableside. He was so warm and friendly, and it made the whole experience both fascinating and delicious. I totally get why their legendary sauce gets its own spot on the menu!
For our entrées, my husband and I both ordered the Petite Filet. They were absolute perfection—honestly, no explanation needed. For our sides, we got the creamed spinach and the mashed potatoes, choosing one each, and neither of them disappointed at all. There wasn't a choice for dessert, so we were given a cookie. I wanted to finish mine at the table, but I was just too full, so I boxed up the rest for the next day. Oh my gosh, it was still incredible!
Our server, Sean, was fantastic and very friendly too, and the restaurant has such a relaxing vibe. (Or maybe I was just extra relaxed after having some wine!) I actually mentioned this to the manager or owner, and he shared an awesome tip with us: wine bottles are half-price on Sundays! I will definitely be back to try more of their steaks on a Sunday (and to try other wines, too!).

Everything was wonderful, with just one minor downside: I wasn't a fan of the automatic 4.50% WeHo Labor surcharge included in the total bill.
